sentences.show: America's most notorious gangster wasn't brought down for murder. It was his taxes.
Al Capone was convicted on this day in 1931.
He ran Chicago's bootlegging empire during Prohibition.
He was widely blamed for the St. Valentine's Day Massacre. But that day, he was in Florida.
So the government went after his money.
The Supreme Court had ruled that even illegal income could be taxed.
Agent Frank Wilson found a ledger, with profits paid to someone called "A".
Worse, Capone's own lawyer had already admitted his income, while offering to pay the tax.
In court, his defence claimed he'd lost it all gambling.
The court heard, at great length, about his spending.
Guilty on five counts. Eleven years in federal prison.
At Alcatraz, the boss of Chicago played banjo in the prison band.
Also on this day: a wave of beer flooded a London street, and a British army surrendered at Saratoga.
